findings.text: The accepted author20 CPU-diagnostic fixture contains an undefined-attribute defect that the prior fixture-correction stage and the controller/synthetic tests did not catch, and it has now caused the second consecutive native failure. In ACCEPTED_AUTHOR20_PRIVATE.py the CPUObserver subclass overrides start() to launch threading.Thread(target=s._sampling_loop,...), but the parent DiagnosticMonitor.start() implements its sampling as a nested local function loop() (there is no method named _sampling_loop anywhere on the class). When the native CPU run reached mon.start() it raised AttributeError: 'CPUObserver' object has no attribute '_sampling_loop' and exited 1. The earlier constructor-only correction (KeyError continue_training) fixed one exception but left the rest of the fixture unaudited; controller/unit passing is insufficient for this native harness. Because this defect is in the accepted scientific fixture, it cannot be papered over with another administrative/field fix and the root must not edit the scientific fixture itself.

rationale:
Independent judgment: REVISE, with PROCEED/SIMPLIFY direction. This is a direction consultation after a genuine SECOND native CPU failure of the already-installed b60badd6 corrected-native stage, not a new code candidate. I confirmed the decisive technical fact directly in the originals: the accepted author20 fixture's CPUObserver.start (ACCEPTED_AUTHOR20_PRIVATE.py:1696) launches a thread targeting s._sampling_loop, which does not exist — the parent DiagnosticMonitor.start (1394-1402) defines sampling as a nested loop(), not a method. The native run failed with exactly that AttributeError (ACTUAL_NATIVE_RESULT_PRIVATE.json; STATUS/outcome exit_code 1, FAIL, UNCERTAIN). This is a real, unresolved code/spec mismatch in the scientific fixture, so APPROVE (which requires empty findings) is unavailable.

REJECT is not warranted because the installed infrastructure behaves correctly and honestly: native_result() requires observed status==VERIFIED and exit_code==0, so the FAIL cannot be forged into a PASS; reviewer16's marker()/verify_delivery depend on that PASS receipt and therefore correctly stay gated (matching the brief's 'reviewer16 held without PASS'); main() writes no_automatic_retry and refuses replay; the failed reservation (1118950) stays UNCERTAIN and fully counted; fixture_correction.failure() qualifies the FAIL without fabricating a PASS; and caps 25M/150M/1200M/1275M plus automatic_retry False and finish_review's always-False execution/coverage/full/global-findings flags are intact. The genuine scientific gate (REVISE15 / DIAG-U2) is preserved.

The prior session's APPROVE of b60badd6 (LATEST_IMPLEMENTATION_AND_DIRECTION.json, packet 10bbb19..., distinct from this binding 528b3d...) was issued before this second failure manifested and is only an ID/hash reference; it is not authority for approving the now-failed state. The correct direction is the brief's shortest author-owned whole-fixture recovery: one scientific author audits and repairs the entire fixture (not just the failing line), adds a fixture-contract test that catches undefined callbacks before any paid native run, preserves all production AST/plan/image/caps/guards, and only then does genuine scientific review judge the correction.
